title: triiiceratops perf-budgets
description: Accepted post-cleanup absolute performance ceilings enforced by scripts/perf/compare.mjs (ticket 25). The comparison job enforces base-vs-head deltas; this file guards absolute drift and fails even when base == head.

baselineRef.description: What was MEASURED to produce this file: a commit SHA, a git ref, or `working-tree` for a --head-root capture. Never inherited from the previous file — inheriting made one stale value self-perpetuating, so regenerations kept naming a ref whose build could not produce the numbers here.

renderer.description: Which renderer the measured dist mounted, detected from the built artifact. `unknown` means no first-party renderer root appeared — a dist predating it, or one whose renderer never mounted — and its numbers are not this renderer's ceilings.

tracing.description: Whether Playwright tracing was on for the runs whose medians these runtime ceilings derive from. Recorded for the same reason as `renderer` — it changes what the numbers mean, not merely their noise: tracing's DOM snapshots cost `activate_image-manipulation` roughly 10x while leaving the load phases alone. `compare.mjs` refuses to enforce these ceilings against a run measured in the other mode, so `--no-traces` on the enforcing job is a checked property of this file rather than a convention.

memoryBytesFloorPct.description: The byte floor a memory regression must also exceed, as a fraction of the BASE reading for that scenario. Proportional rather than flat: a flat floor has to be sized for the largest scenario, and at 4 MiB it exceeded the entire thumbnail-tier measurement — so a thumbnail rung 256 -> 512 regression (a 4x increase in decoded bytes) cleared every gate.

memoryBytesFloorMinBytes.description: Lower bound on the proportional byte floor, so a near-zero baseline does not make the gate hair-trigger.

memoryAbsTiles.description: Absolute resident-tile increase a memory regression must also exceed.

acceptedSizeIncreases.description: Reviewed exemptions from the base-vs-head size gate. An artifact listed here may exceed the +5% delta as long as its head size stays at or below `headBytes`. Use only for intentional cost shifts (e.g. work moving from an external dependency into first-party code, which the base measurement never counted). Delete the entry once main carries the new cost, so the ordinary gate resumes.

headBytes.description: Maximum accepted head size in bytes. A head larger than this fails even with the exemption.

runtime.description: Per-scenario median ceilings in milliseconds (captured median with noise headroom).

memory.description: Per-scenario renderer residency ceilings, fed by the renderer's OWN counters and not by a browser heap metric: decoded tiles are ImageBitmaps living outside the JS heap, so a heap ceiling reads near-flat while tiles leak. Measured against the generated 800-canvas continuous fixture. A budgeted scenario that produces no counters fails rather than passing, so a dist built without the Canvas2D renderer cannot slip through; a MEASURED scenario with no entry here fails too, so the object being present but empty cannot pass as enforcement. Always emitted, empty when nothing was measured (a `--size-only` capture), because a missing key wrote a file this schema rejects.

residentTileCount.description: Tiles held in the required set once the traverse has settled. The load-bearing counter: the required set is never evicted, so this is where a residency leak shows up.

requiredBytes.description: The required set alone, in decoded bytes. Budgeted because it is the only counter that moves when the residency tier or the thumbnail rung changes and nothing else does: a rung regression resolves the SAME canvases at twice the size, so residentTileCount is unchanged, and decodedBytes carries the opportunistic cache's jitter.

decodedBytes.description: Required set plus opportunistic cache — the total the scheduler's byte budget governs.

ceilingDecodedBytes.description: Must stay BELOW `byteBudget`: above it, the scheduler's own trim() already guarantees the bound and this ceiling asserts nothing. compare.mjs reports that as a failure.

byteBudget.description: The decoded-byte ceiling in force during the measurement (the shipped desktop default, per ADR 0014). Recorded for context and to validate ceilingDecodedBytes; not itself enforced.
